title: In God's Own House Pronounce His Praise
description: In God's Own House Pronounce His Praise in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 150, headed “A song of praise”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: In God's own house pro-nounce his praise, His grace he there re-veals; To heaven your joy and won-der raise, For there his glo-ry dwells.

lines: In God's own house pronounce his praise,
To heaven your joy and wonder raise,
Let all your sacred passions move,
But the great work of saving love
All that have motion, life, and breath,
Yet when my voice expires in death,
My soul shall praise him best.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
